messages.author: d9598e914e37c995
messages.subject: Applying biogeobears to migration strategies
parts:
Hi all,
I am currently trying to use BiogeoBEARS to estimate ancestral bird migration strategies (resident, migrant or partial migrant) to understand the evolutionary origins of long distance migration behaviours.

To do so, from species distribution maps, I'm coding range colors for each species (Yellow=Breeding range, Green=Resident range, Blue= Wintering range), and from there, I define the current migration strategies : (Yellow / Blue) for an exclusively migrant species, (Green) for a resident species or (Yellow/Green/Blue),(Yellow/Green),(Green/Blue) for a partial migrant species.

From there, I would like to reconstruct the ancestral strategies, but I encountered a major problem: the ancestors should not be present in a single range of only yellow (breeding range) or only blue range (wintering range), as it is biologically impossible.
Is there a way in BioGeoBEARs to provide this information, i.e. to set to zero the probability of certain ancestral states?

Thank you very much for your help,

Paul

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Applying biogeobears to migration strategies
parts:
Hi,

This is an interesting question. You can manually edit the states_list to remove some states (search the group on that phrase), but I think you also have to think very carefully about the transitions you allow in the state space, which would not be identical with the transitions allowed in the standard BioGeoBEARS models.

Hopefully you have seen the clever paper, I think by Winger, Ree, et al., on exactly this kind of model? It was in PNAS. I think they used custom code that hasn't been released (I might be wrong). I can imagine programming such a model for BioGeoBEARS, but it would be A Somewhat Major Project, and I don't know how long it would be before I would have time.  But feel free to email me if you want to explore that possibility though.

Cheers!
Nick
